requirement: Compiler-centered local agentic orchestration framework
description: The system is a local-first orchestration framework that transforms prompts into structured workflows compiled to Rust for execution.
outputs: Workflow spec, executable plan, artifacts, responses
implications: Requires deterministic compilation, inspectable workflows, local-first design
acceptance_tests: Given a prompt, the system generates a YAML workflow and compiled Rust code that runs locally to produce the expected output.

requirement: Open-source hacker vibe with short
description: memorable naming
inputs: The project should feel like hacker infrastructure: transparent, modifiable, and scriptable with a short, memorable name.
implications: Project name, repository and crate names
source_basis: Encourages permissive license, pluggable architecture, CLI-first design
acceptance_tests: p2
dependencies: Project repository and crates are publicly accessible under an open-source license and the binary name is under three syllables.

requirement: Local-first execution
description: storage
outputs: The system runs on machines owned by the user, storing and executing workflows locally without relying on cloud services.
implications: Local models, local files, local hardware
status: Necessitates local model runners, local storage, offline mode, privacy controls
acceptance_tests: explicit
notes: System can execute a workflow end-to-end without internet connectivity, using local models and storing outputs in the local .glyphnova directory.

requirement: Depth over speed and capability-normalized outcomes
description: Weaker hardware may achieve similar results by running deeper, longer workflows with more summarization and verification.
implications: Requires capability-aware compilation, summarization, retrieval loops, multi-pass review
acceptance_tests: Given a low-memory device profile, the compiled workflow uses chunked context and additional summarization steps but yields functionally correct results compared to a high-memory profile.

requirement: CLI-first with future Tauri/React UI
description: Start with a robust CLI and optional TUI, then evolve into a Tauri/React desktop UI while preserving core abstractions.
implications: Promotes separation between runtime and UI, headless support, plugin design
acceptance_tests: CLI allows creating chats, queuing runs, inspecting statuses; TUI shows queue; UI integration is optional and built on same runtime.

requirement: Evolution toward always-on autonomous local agents
description: The system should eventually support persistent agents that run continuously on local hardware, performing tasks over time.
implications: Requires background scheduling, persistent state, long-running loops, periodic summarization
acceptance_tests: After enabling longtail mode, the system can run tasks in the background across restarts and produce periodic reports.

requirement: Each chat is a scoped executable work container
description: Chats are not just message logs; they contain state, folder scope, queue status, artifacts, and associated workflows.
implications: Requires ChatSession abstraction, persistent storage of context, per-chat folder
acceptance_tests: When a new chat is created, a folder and .glyphnova directory are created; messages and runs remain associated with this chat.

requirement: Visible queue of chats with statuses and priorities
description: The UI (CLI/TUI/UI) should display chats as a queue with titles, statuses and priorities; queue is interactive.
outputs: Visual queue listing, actions (reprioritize, pause, resume)
implications: Requires queue abstraction, status semantics, interactive commands
acceptance_tests: Users can view chat queue with statuses and reorder items; reordering affects scheduling.

requirement: Drag-and-drop or commands to reprioritize chats/workflows
description: Users can reorder the queue to change execution priorities; scheduler respects new ordering.
implications: Requires safe pause points; scheduler should reschedule tasks; logs update
acceptance_tests: Reordering a chat moves it to the desired position and scheduler picks it up accordingly without data corruption.

requirement: Provide nested topics
description: nested summaries and graph views
inputs: Users should navigate conversation through topics, summaries and graph views; not just linear logs.
outputs: Chat logs, workflow graphs, topic extraction
implications: Topic trees, summary levels, graph visualizations
source_basis: Requires summary pipelines, graph generation, indexing
acceptance_tests: p2
dependencies: Topic extraction generates tree; user can click topics to view messages; graph view shows dependencies; summary view displays condensed information.

requirement: Visible scope and explicit context switch confirmation
description: Current folder scope must always be visible and changes require user confirmation; no hidden scope switch.
implications: Requires scope tracking and gating, prompts to user
acceptance_tests: When a workflow requests a different folder, the user is asked to confirm; if denied, operation fails; scope indicator updates accordingly.

requirement: Control runtime
description: review cycles
implications: concurrency
status: Expose sliders or numeric inputs to adjust runtime expectation, number of review cycles, criticality level, scope enforcement, concurrency and efficiency preferences.
acceptance_tests: RunPolicy
dependencies: Compiler must convert slider settings into budgets, gating density, concurrency, model choice, summarization frequency
column17: Slider adjustments change behaviour; e.g., increasing review cycles results in additional verify-repair loops in the compiled workflow.

requirement: More clarification and confirmation for long or high-risk runs
description: The system should increase the number of clarification prompts and confirmation checkpoints as runtime length or risk increases.
implications: Compiler inserts clarifier nodes and gating functions; scheduler pauses waiting for user input
acceptance_tests: In longtail mode, before executing actions on files, the user is asked to confirm; in ASAP mode fewer prompts appear.

requirement: Category-sensitive workflow shapes and prioritization
description: Different categories (quick answer, deep research, continuous improvement) map to different templates and scheduling strategies.
implications: Requires template library, classifier; influences queueing and concurrency
acceptance_tests: Requests labelled 'cron job' compile into scheduled recurring tasks; direct questions compile into short workflows.

requirement: Schema-based YAML DSL for agentic behaviour
description: Workflows must be defined in a typed YAML format with nodes for steps, tools, models, review loops, and effects.
implications: Enables linting, type checks, deterministic code generation; fosters shareable workflows
acceptance_tests: Workflow definitions must validate successfully against the schema; invalid structures produce errors.

requirement: Prompt to YAML workflow generation
description: Prompts must first be transformed into YAML workflows before execution; planning is explicit.
implications: Separates planning from execution; yields inspectable plan
acceptance_tests: When given a task, the system outputs a YAML file with steps; user can view and edit it before execution.

requirement: Multiple workflow archetypes and modes
description: Provide several canonical workflow shapes: direct answer, plan-then-answer, plan-execute-verify, iterative refinement, continuous loops, and cron jobs.
implications: Compiler must implement various templates, handle each mode
acceptance_tests: Selecting 'plan-execute-verify' results in a workflow with explicit planning, execution and verification nodes; selecting 'cron' yields a scheduled recurring plan.

requirement: Tools and custom Rust tools as first-class nodes
description: The DSL should allow specifying tool invocations with typed inputs and outputs, including custom Rust tool calls beyond the base AgentSDK.
implications: Requires tool registry, typed contracts, plugin API
acceptance_tests: Tools defined in YAML compile into Rust trait calls; custom tools implement required traits and integrate into generated code.

requirement: Explicit DAG/state-machine semantics and composability
description: Workflows should be represented as graphs/state machines with named steps, typed edges and explicit transitions.
implications: Enables deterministic compilation, graph visualisation, reuse of sub-flows
acceptance_tests: The compiled IR produces a deterministic adjacency list; cycles are disallowed or explicitly annotated; graph can be visualized.

requirement: Declared effects and preflight
description: Workflows should declare intended files, tools, models, and scopes before execution to allow preview and gating.
implications: Enables diff staging, user approval, safe context transitions
acceptance_tests: Before executing a workflow, the system produces a list of files it will touch; user can approve or deny.

requirement: Workflows are inspectable and editable artifacts
description: Generated YAML files are stored, versioned, and editable; they can be reused or modified by subsequent workflows.
implications: Facilitates reproducibility, sharing, library of workflows, meta-workflows
acceptance_tests: After a workflow is generated, the YAML file can be opened and edited; modifications produce new versions.

requirement: Whitt Execution Engine compilation target
description: YAML workflow specs must compile to Rust code targeting the AgentSDK or a runtime trait; code is deterministic and typed.
implications: Requires code generation modules, stable runtime API, version compatibility
acceptance_tests: Given a YAML workflow and installed Rust toolchain, the compiler generates a buildable crate; cargo build produces a binary that executes the plan.

requirement: Support multiple packaging strategies (standalone
description: import backend
outputs: Generated Rust code can be packaged as a standalone project, rely on a backend crate, or inline the backend; strategy chosen based on environment.
implications: Packaging config
status: Tradeoff between duplication, update ease, distribution; must be configurable
acceptance_tests: expanded
notes: User can select packaging strategy; generated output matches; packaging can compile with minimal dependencies.

requirement: Queue semantics
description: worker pools
implications: The runtime scheduler must handle priority scheduling, concurrency, persistence of queues, cancellation, retries, and result reporting.
priority: Needs persistent queue storage, worker threads or async tasks, state machine
acceptance_tests: Windmill;job_scheduler;work_queue
column15: Jobs enqueued persist across restarts; concurrency can be configured; canceled jobs stop at safe checkpoints; results are collected.

requirement: Generate → verify → repair cycles
description: Runtime executes generate, verify, and repair steps based on review depth and criticality policies.
implications: Requires verifiers, repair mechanisms, iterative loop control
acceptance_tests: For an intentionally faulty output, the system enters a repair loop until the verifier passes or the review limit is reached.

requirement: Background
description: semi-endless
outputs: Workflows can run indefinitely or in scheduled loops; they must be pausable and resumable across restarts.
implications: Longtail mode, cron schedule
acceptance_tests: explicit
notes: Cron job runs at scheduled intervals; stopping the process and restarting resumes the job from last checkpoint.

requirement: Progressive results for interactive runs
description: ASAP mode should stream partial outputs while deeper work continues in longtail; user gets immediate results and eventual final outputs.
implications: Requires streaming, progressive synthesis, intermediate artifact updates
acceptance_tests: When requesting an answer, the system returns a quick first draft, then later sends refined results; user sees incremental updates.

requirement: Each chat has a scope root folder
description: All operations in a chat occur within its directory; prevents cross-chat file interference.
implications: Path access must be restricted; UI shows path
acceptance_tests: File operations outside the chat root are blocked unless scope is changed; operations inside succeed.

requirement: Create a .glyphnova directory within each scope for artifacts
description: The system stores logs, workflow specs, intermediate files, summaries, graphs, reports, and run metadata in a hidden .glyphnova directory.
implications: Requires versioning, schema for artifact types, storage structure
acceptance_tests: After executing a workflow, the .glyphnova directory contains the workflow file, logs, traces, diff proposals, reports.

requirement: Support multiple logging levels
description: Users can choose how detailed logs should be: from light summaries to full trace; logging policy influences storage and context budgets.
implications: Logging consumes storage; summarization must preserve essential info
acceptance_tests: Setting logging to summary mode stores only high-level events; trace mode stores per-node details; context assembly picks from logs accordingly.

requirement: File changes should be proposed as diffs and applied after approval
description: All file creations, edits, or deletions are prepared as diffs; user can approve or auto-apply based on policy; rollback strategy exists.
implications: Requires diff library, patch application, backup storage
acceptance_tests: Before editing a file, the system shows a unified diff; after approval, the diff is applied; if denied, no changes occur.

requirement: Generate human-readable reports from artifacts
description: The system should produce readable reports summarising runs, requirements, research, benchmarking, evaluation with support for markdown and exported formats.
implications: Requires templating, summarization, script integration
acceptance_tests: After a run, the system can generate a markdown report summarising the steps, tool results and final outputs into the docs folder.

requirement: Provide structured traces for each node
description: Each node execution should record inputs, outputs, timings, failures, and retries; traces stored in artifacts.
implications: Requires instrumentation, structured logging, time stamping, ID tagging
acceptance_tests: After executing a workflow, there is a trace file per node containing a structured log of its inputs and outputs.

requirement: Generate workflow and topic graphs
description: System must produce Graphviz or similar graph files representing workflows and topics for navigation and introspection.
implications: Requires graph generation and serialization; separate graph types
acceptance_tests: Graph files exist in .glyphnova; they can be rendered into diagrams; nodes correspond to workflow steps or topics.

requirement: Standard status vocabulary across UI and CLI
description: Define states such as queued, running, blocked, verifying, repairing, completed, failed, canceled; store transitions in artifacts.
implications: UI and CLI must present statuses consistently; scheduler must update statuses
acceptance_tests: At any time, a run shows one of the defined statuses; state transitions are recorded and can be audited.

requirement: Support multiple local model backends via provider abstraction
description: Allow using various local LLM frameworks such as llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM/Ollama, text-generation-webui; unify via a provider interface.
implications: Requires common API, ability to query capabilities like context length, tokenization, streaming, tool-calling
acceptance_tests: Switching provider between llama.cpp and vLLM yields similar outputs with proper API calls; provider reports its capabilities.

requirement: Load
description: unload
inputs: warm up and manage multiple model instances
outputs: Runtime must load models into memory on demand, unload them to free memory, and manage multiple instances concurrently.
implications: Model id, memory budgets
status: Requires memory accounting, instance pooling, concurrency control
acceptance_tests: explicit
notes: Loading a model decreases available memory; unloading releases memory; running two instances concurrently uses separate threads or processes.

requirement: Run multiple instances of the same model or different models concurrently
description: Allow parallel tasks by running multiple models or instances; plan concurrency according to memory and hardware.
implications: Needs concurrency scheduler, memory accounting, thread or process management
acceptance_tests: Two summarization tasks run concurrently on separate model instances; tasks complete faster than sequential execution without memory error.

requirement: Use small models for planning and big models for difficult tasks
description: Assign different roles (planner, checker, synthesizer) to models based on their strengths and resource needs; small models handle simple tasks; bigger models handle complex tasks.
implications: Requires classification of tasks, model capability matrix, dynamic routing in compilation
acceptance_tests: Planner tasks use a small model; synthesizer tasks use a large model; compiled workflow shows different model nodes accordingly.

requirement: Manage context by summarizing
description: retrieving
outputs: Since models have finite context, system must assemble prompts from history, summaries, retrieval results, tool logs, and artifacts; no hidden memory beyond explicit context.
implications: History, summaries, artifacts, retrieval queries
status: Requires summarization pipelines, retrieval search, context budget policies
acceptance_tests: expanded
notes: Long conversations remain summarised; context builder uses summaries instead of raw logs; there is no memory leak or unlimited context.

requirement: Adapt workflow planning based on context length and memory pressure
description: Plan segmentation, summarization frequency, and chunk sizes must be adjusted according to hardware memory and context length to avoid OOM.
implications: Compiler must compute available context budget, cut tasks into segments, summarise more aggressively on weak devices
acceptance_tests: On an 8GB device, tasks are broken into smaller steps with summarization; on a high-end GPU, tasks can run with longer contexts.

requirement: Evaluate whether GPU offloading improves performance considering memory bandwidth and overhead
description: GPU offloading is not always faster; system should decide offload levels based on model size, context and hardware; CPU may outperform GPU for small contexts.
inputs: Model size, context length, hardware memory bandwidth
implications: Requires benchmarks, heuristics; tune CPU/GPU layers; hybrid compute
acceptance_tests: System selects CPU-only for small models; GPU offloading for large models; performance logs show improvement accordingly.

requirement: Maintain structured descriptions of devices with memory
description: CPU/GPU resources
outputs: Each node's capabilities (RAM, VRAM, CPU, GPU, installed models, tools, concurrency caps) are registered to inform compilation and scheduling.
implications: Device probes, manual config
status: Scheduler chooses devices; compiler tailors workflows
acceptance_tests: explicit
notes: Registering a new device populates fields; compiled workflow adjusts to device capabilities (e.g., uses smaller model).

requirement: Dispatch subwork across devices based on capabilities and load
description: For distributed local swarm, tasks can run on different nodes; results are merged and synchronized.
implications: Requires task partitioning, remote execution API, artifact synchronization, network resilience
acceptance_tests: A workflow step requiring a GPU is dispatched to a desktop; a summarization step runs on a phone; results integrate seamlessly.

requirement: Survive interruptions and reassign tasks across nodes
description: Longtail or continuous workflows must survive node failures; tasks can be resumed from checkpoints on another device.
implications: Requires robust checkpointing, idempotent tasks, detection of node failures, reassigning tasks
acceptance_tests: If a device goes offline mid-run, tasks are resumed on another device using checkpoint data; final results match expected output.

requirement: Benchmark models
description: devices and context lengths to inform routing and scheduling
inputs: The system should provide tasks to measure performance (latency, throughput, failure rates) across hardware and model configurations.
implications: Metrics artifacts
source_basis: Helps build capability profiles, tune heuristics; should store results in artifacts and produce charts.
acceptance_tests: p2
dependencies: Running a benchmark suite yields metrics for each model-device combination; results are stored and used to inform decisions.

requirement: Produce radar/spider/web/bar charts for metrics
description: System should generate charts summarising evaluation metrics to help users compare models, devices and workflows.
implications: Requires charting library, templates; charts saved as images or interactive HTML
acceptance_tests: After running benchmarks, the system produces charts (PNG/SVG) showing throughput vs latency across models.

requirement: Optional compute-sharing and discoverability
description: Future versions may allow nodes to expose resources for sharing tasks; tasks dispatched externally may award tokens or credits.
implications: Requires security, reputation system, network protocols; optional features for community compute sharing
acceptance_tests: Not applicable yet; design specification required for marketplace feature.

requirement: Registry of deterministic tools for diffing
description: formatting
implications: building
status: Maintain a registry of available tools with typed input/output signatures, permission controls and logging.
acceptance_tests: Tool results, errors
dependencies: Requires plugin interface, tool discovery, versioning; fosters deterministic behaviour outside model
column17: Tools are discoverable via registry; tool calls produce structured results; unauthorized tool calls are blocked.

requirement: Ability to add custom Rust tools beyond base AgentSDK
description: Developers can write new Rust tools implementing defined traits and register them for use in workflows.
implications: Requires trait definition, dynamic loading or linking, safety checks, sandboxing
acceptance_tests: Adding a new tool crate and registering it allows the YAML to call it; tool executes with proper inputs and returns typed outputs.

requirement: Provide clear local installation story and upgrade paths
description: User can install the system via binary or package; generation process may also output self-contained workflow projects; upgrades should handle migrations and schema changes.
implications: Requires packaging scripts, version management, upgrade path
acceptance_tests: Using the installer sets up the CLI with dependencies; running upgrade preserves existing chats and workflows; outdated artifacts are migrated.

requirement: Standardize repository structure for transpiler
description: runtime
implications: Define clear folder structure: crates for transpiler, runtime, CLI; docs; opencode integration; schemas; examples.
acceptance_tests: Matrix;CrabNebula
column15: Repository root contains crates folder, transpiler, runtime, CLI; docs; opencode folder; build scripts reference correct paths.

requirement: Generate extensive report suites from requirements via scripts
description: Scripts parse requirements CSV and produce multiple markdown reports for OpenCode: glossary, architecture mapping, project comparison, performance guide, schema options, security model, evaluation plan.
implications: Requires script plan, template engine, crosslinker
acceptance_tests: Running the scripts generates expected .md files under ./transpiler/opencode/docs/reports/requirements-research-and-documentation/ with correct content.

requirement: Define canonical YAML grammar for workflows
description: Establish a formal schema specifying node types, fields, constraints, and versioning for YAML workflows.
implications: Enables validation, auto-completion, tool integration; must support evolution.
acceptance_tests: Workflows validate against the schema; invalid fields raise errors; schema supports new versions via migrations.

requirement: Provide migration tooling to upgrade old workflow specs to new schema versions
description: Maintain version history and scripts to transform workflows when schema changes; store migration metadata in artifacts.
inputs: Old schema version, new schema version, migration scripts
implications: Ensures backward compatibility; supports concurrency between versions
acceptance_tests: Given a workflow from schema v1, applying migration to v2 transforms fields appropriately; after migration, validation passes.

requirement: Validate YAML workflows for required fields
description: types and constraints before compilation
inputs: Validation should catch missing fields, wrong types, invalid schedules, cycles, permission violations and produce actionable errors.
implications: Validation report
source_basis: Prevents runtime errors, ensures compliance; must be part of compile phase
acceptance_tests: p0
dependencies: Submitting an incomplete YAML returns validation errors describing missing fields; fixed YAML passes.

requirement: Offer lint rules and suggestions for improved reliability and readability
description: Linting should warn about missing timeouts, ambiguous names, unbounded loops, or unapproved file operations; suggestions should be actionable.
implications: Encourages best practices; separate from validation; can be configured to warnings or errors
acceptance_tests: A workflow missing timeouts triggers a lint warning; adjusting the YAML resolves the warning.

requirement: Parse YAML into an internal AST with stable node identities and typed fields
description: The parser must preserve location data for error messages and assign stable identifiers for nodes used in graph building.
implications: Facilitates cross-references, graph building, error reporting
acceptance_tests: Parsing a YAML file produces an AST containing nodes with unique IDs and line numbers; no lost information.

requirement: Convert AST into a typed intermediate representation suitable for graph building and code generation
description: The IR should include typed edges, explicit state structures, policy bindings and effect declarations; graphable and deterministic.
implications: Enables deterministic codegen, normalization, caching
acceptance_tests: Converting a valid AST yields a WorkflowIR with typed nodes and edges; IR can be traversed as a graph.

requirement: Normalize IR into canonical form with stable sorting and IDs
description: Ensures identical inputs produce identical IRs; eliminates nondeterministic ordering; supports caching and diffing.
implications: Facilitates reproducible builds and caching
acceptance_tests: Running the compiler twice on same YAML produces identical IR and code; difference only depends on input, not runtime conditions.

requirement: Map IR concepts to Rust AgentSDK traits and functions
description: Implement a layer that converts IR nodes to calls on the AgentSDK runtime: agent creation, tool calls, state management, scheduling hooks.
implications: Requires adapter traits; ensures compiled code is maintainable and testable
acceptance_tests: Generated code compiles against AgentSDK crate and runs the workflow correctly.

requirement: Generate code to bind YAML-declared tools to Rust trait implementations
description: For each tool call in YAML, code must handle serialization/deserialization, cancellation, permission checks and logging.
implications: Requires typed tool interfaces and adapter code; ensures safe execution
acceptance_tests: Generated Rust code for a tool call correctly serializes inputs, calls the tool, and handles errors; user-defined tools integrate seamlessly.

requirement: Generate Cargo project structure per compiled workflow
description: Outputs a directory with Cargo.toml, src files, modules and build metadata; ensures consistent layout for building and packaging.
implications: Makes distribution and building easier; supports versioning
acceptance_tests: Compilation outputs a directory with expected files; cargo build in that directory produces the binary.

requirement: Choose packaging strategy per run: standalone
description: import backend
outputs: Strategy determines whether generated code includes all dependencies, references the runtime crate or inlines the runtime; must be configurable.
implications: User or policy preference
status: Impacts binary size, portability, update mechanism
acceptance_tests: implied
notes: Selecting 'inline' produces code with runtime logic included; 'import' references installed crate; 'standalone' includes runtime crate as dependency.

requirement: Generate hooks for scheduler integration: run IDs
description: checkpoints
outputs: Insert code to track progress, update statuses, persist checkpoints, and produce artifact outputs; integrate with scheduler and .glyphnova.
implications: WorkflowIR, runtime contract
status: Provides run introspection; ensures persistent state across restarts
acceptance_tests: explicit
notes: Generated code includes calls to update run status, persist checkpoint data to artifacts and to produce logs; scheduler responds accordingly.

requirement: Emit preflight effect reports listing files
description: scopes
implications: Before compilation or at compile time, produce effect reports for review and gating; ensures tasks are transparent.
priority: Supports gating and diff staging; ensures declarations match actual plan
acceptance_tests: Matrix
column15: Compilation outputs an effect report listing expected file writes; difference between declared and actual usage triggers an error.

requirement: Generate call sites for verifiers based on review loops
description: Code generation must embed calls to verification modules (schema, diff, test) at appropriate points; verifiers are pluggable.
implications: Enables modular verification; ensures runtime honours review loops
acceptance_tests: If a verification step fails, the generated code triggers repair loop or fails gracefully; verifiers can be swapped.

requirement: Use consistent formatting for generated Rust code
description: Ensure code uses stable formatting and ordering to minimize diffs; run rustfmt with pinned toolchain.
implications: Improves readability, diffing, caching; ensures reproducibility
acceptance_tests: Running code generation twice yields identical output; rustfmt runs; modules appear in consistent order.

requirement: Provide reproducible build steps with pinned toolchain and dependencies
description: Generated projects should include Cargo.lock and specify Rust version; builds should work offline if caches are available.
implications: Ensures consistent builds; facilitates reproducibility and offline building
acceptance_tests: Running cargo build yields same binary; using offline mode still builds when dependencies exist; recorded metadata is correct.

requirement: Provide golden/snapshot tests for YAML to Rust generation
description: Maintain sample YAML inputs with expected generated code; use snapshot testing to detect regressions.
implications: Ensures deterministic code generation; catches accidental changes
acceptance_tests: Running test suite compares generated outputs with snapshots; differences highlight regressions; tests pass when outputs match.

requirement: Stress test parser
description: validator and normalizer with randomized inputs
inputs: Use property-based testing to explore edge cases; ensure parser and validation handle arbitrary but valid or invalid YAML structures.
implications: Failing cases / minimized repro
acceptance_tests: p3
dependencies: Randomly generated valid YAML always parses and validates; invalid structures produce expected errors; test harness finds no panics.

requirement: Cache compiled results based on inputs and environment
description: Avoid recompiling identical workflows; use hashes of YAML, schema version, toolchain and backend contract to look up cached code.
implications: Improves performance; ensures cache invalidation when environment changes
acceptance_tests: Recompiling a workflow with unchanged inputs uses the cache; modifying the schema or toolchain invalidates the cache.

requirement: Ensure code generation cannot write outside allowed paths or import unsafe dependencies
description: Treat YAML as untrusted input; enforce allowlists for file generation and external crates; ensure path guards.
implications: Prevents injection or path traversal; ensures compiled code is safe
acceptance_tests: Malicious YAML trying to write outside the project directory fails; generated code imports only approved crates; path guard error is reported.

requirement: Lower high-level workflow nodes into different IR structures based on capability profile
description: Transpiler must transform high-level constructs into device-specific forms (e.g., dividing tasks into smaller pieces for low-memory devices).
implications: Improves portability; ensures tasks fit available resources
acceptance_tests: When compiling for a phone, large loops are split; when compiling for a desktop, tasks remain intact; outputs produce correct results.

requirement: Generate documentation from schema definitions
description: Automatically produce reference docs for each node type, field, and example usage; show version changes.
implications: Improves developer adoption; reduces guesswork
acceptance_tests: Running documentation generator outputs markdown or HTML docs listing each node type, field descriptions, allowed values and examples; docs update after schema changes.

requirement: Provide repository and file awareness
description: integrating with editors and language servers
inputs: The system should integrate with project files, understanding dependencies, syntax errors, and file tree; support LSP features.
implications: Context-aware prompts and analysis
source_basis: Needs indexing of files, integration with LSP or language tooling, cross-references
acceptance_tests: p2
dependencies: When editing code in an editor, the assistant refers to correct file paths and symbols; CLI suggests file names.

requirement: Headless execution and CI-friendly integration
description: System can run workflows without human interaction; output machine-readable logs; integrate into build pipelines or automation scripts.
inputs: CLI commands, plan files, environment variables
implications: Allows scheduled tasks, integration into pipelines; emphasises clear exit codes
acceptance_tests: Running a workflow with CLI flags such as --non-interactive completes without prompts; output includes status codes; automation script uses return values.

requirement: Safe defaults with conservative policies
description: Default settings emphasize safety: confirm before high-impact actions, restrict scope, log events; user must explicitly relax them.
implications: Prevents accidental data loss; fosters trust
acceptance_tests: On first run, modifications to files always require approval; enabling 'auto-apply' is an explicit opt-in.

requirement: Maintain coherent abstraction stack from philosophy to runtime primitives
description: The architecture must align high-level philosophy (local-first, safety) with defined primitives and runtime behaviours; names and behaviours should match the conceptual model.
implications: Improves maintainability; reduces cognitive load; fosters spec compliance
acceptance_tests: Documentation and code show clear mapping between ChatSession, Scope, RunPolicy etc. and high-level concepts; there are no hidden states.

requirement: Support background workflows to revisit artifacts and improve results over time
description: The system should run meta-workflows that analyze logs, files, and run history to produce new insights, refactor code, improve prompts or refine workflows.
implications: Encourages continuous improvement; requires scheduled tasks, summarization, evaluation
acceptance_tests: After a run, a background process analyses the results and suggests improvements; improvements appear in subsequent runs.

requirement: Define unresolved design decisions: exact YAML grammar
description: AgentSDK target shape
implications: commit model
status: Identify and resolve open design questions necessary for a stable v1; document tradeoffs and options.
acceptance_tests: Decisions document
dependencies: Prevents feature creep; clarifies road map
column17: Design doc lists options and decisions for each open question; after consensus, update schema and implementation accordingly.

requirement: Provide a concise description of the entire system
description: Craft a single sentence capturing the essence of the local-first agentic orchestration framework for communications and documentation.
implications: Helps marketing, design alignment; ensures everyone understands goal
acceptance_tests: Documentation includes a one-sentence summary that resonates with stakeholders.
